# 🛡️ Autonomous Credit Risk Scoring System & MLOps Pipeline

This repository contains the complete end-to-end source code, configurations, and documentation for an **Autonomous Credit Risk Scoring System & MLOps Pipeline** (Tugas Akhir / Final Project). 

The system integrates synthetic data generation, statistical feature engineering (Weight of Evidence), class imbalance correction (SMOTE), robust model training (XGBoost with Monotonic Constraints), privacy & utility verification (TSTR Quality Gate), interactive API serving (FastAPI with SHAP explainability), and MLOps automation (n8n + drift monitoring).

---

## 🏗️ System Architecture & Data Lifecycle

The end-to-end architecture is designed as a closed-loop automated system where model inference feedback, data drift checking, and retraining occur systematically.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph DataGen [1. Data Generation & Preprocessing]
        A[GenerateData.py] -->|Synthetic Credit Risk Data| B(synthetic_credit_risk_data.csv)
        B --> C[WoETransformer]
        C -->|12 selected features with IV > 0.02| D[SmoteResampler]
        D -->|Balanced Classes 50/50| E[X_train_final / y_train_res]
    end

    subgraph MLOpsGate [2. Quality Gate & Evaluation]
        F[evaluate_tstr.py] -->|Fidelity Check| G[Inverted KS Statistic]
        F -->|Privacy Check| H[Distance to Closest Record - DCR]
        F -->|Utility Validation| I[TSTR vs. TRTR Comparison]
        I -->|If AUC Drop > 10%| J[Flag: Low Utility]
        I -->|If AUC Drop <= 10%| K[Pass Quality Gate]
    end

    subgraph ModelOps [3. Model Registry & Serve]
        L[trainingCredit.py] -->|Hyperparameter Tune: RandomizedSearchCV| M[XGBClassifier]
        M -->|ROC AUC > 0.70| N[MLflow Run & Registry]
        N -->|Transition stage to| O[Production Stage]
        O -->|Lazy load artifacts| P[FastAPI serving/app.py]
    end

    subgraph Client [4. Web Application & UI]
        P -->|Exposes REST API| Q[FastAPI Endpoints]
        Q -->|Web Dashboard| R[HTML5/CSS3/JS Single-Page UI]
        R -->|Manual Form / Bulk CSV Upload| S[Request payload to /predict]
        S -->|Returns risk grades, proba, SHAP drivers| R
    end

    subgraph AutoLoop [5. Drift Monitoring & Retraining]
        Q -->|Log predictions| T[inference_logs.jsonl]
        U[n8n Scheduler] -->|Weekly trigger| V[check_triggers.py]
        V -->|Loads ref snapshot vs.| T
        V -->|Calculates CSI per feature| W{Is CSI > 0.25?}
        W -->|Yes: Drift Detected| X[Trigger n8n Webhook]
        X -->|Executes training pipeline| L
        W -->|No| Y[Sleep / No Action]
    end

    B -.-> F
    E --> L
    K --> N
```

## 📂 Project Directory Structure

Below is a detailed layout of the files and directories inside this workspace:

It generates expectation variables like `PD`, `LGD`, `EAD`, and the target `missed_payment_flag`.
    *   [`trainingCredit.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/ModelTraining/trainingCredit.py): The core training script. Applies WoE selection, SMOTE resampling, performs a `RandomizedSearchCV` hyperparameter sweep, registers models in MLflow if `AUC > 0.70`, and automatically promotes the best version to `Production`.
    *   [`check_triggers.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/ModelTraining/check_triggers.py): Evaluates whether retraining is required based on model age (>90 days), macroeconomic indicator spikes, or data drift (CSI > 0.25).

    *   [`feature_selection.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/feature_selection.py): Implements a custom class [`WoETransformer`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/feature_selection.py#L30) to compute Weight of Evidence (WoE) and Information Value (IV), filter low-predictive features, and reduce non-linear boundaries.
    *   [`imbalance_handler.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/imbalance_handler.py): Implements [`SmoteResampler`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/imbalance_handler.py#L18) using SMOTE to handle minority default class imbalances.
    *   [`drift_monitor.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/drift_monitor.py): Implements [`DriftMonitor`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/drift_monitor.py#L55) to calculate Population Stability Index (PSI) and Characteristic Stability Index (CSI) with log epsilon smoothing.
*   **[`TSTR/`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/TSTR/) (Quality Gate Validation)**
    *   [`evaluate_tstr.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/TSTR/evaluate_tstr.py): Orchestrates the Train Synthetic Test Real (TSTR) vs. Train Real Test Real (TRTR) comparison. Logs metrics in MLflow.

    *   [`app.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/serving/app.py): FastAPI backend. Lazy-loads the `Production` model and its corresponding WoE transformer from the MLflow Artifact Registry. Integrates `shap.TreeExplainer` with a list-like base score workaround for local feature attribution on `/predict`.
    *   [`static/`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/serving/static/): Single-page static UI for interacting with predictions.
        *   [`index.html`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/serving/static/index.html): Standard structure dashboard with sidebar.

## 🛠️ Detailed Module Breakdown

### 1. Preprocessing System ([`preprocessing/`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/preprocessing/))

*   **`WoETransformer`**: Encodes continuous and high-cardinality categorical variables. For each bin or category, it calculates:
    $$\text{WoE}_i = \ln\left( \frac{\%\text{ Good}}{\%\text{ Bad}} \right)$$
    The Information Value (IV) is used to score predicting capabilities:
    $$\text{IV} = \sum (\%\text{ Good} - \%\text{ Bad}) \times \text{WoE}_i$$
    *Interpretation: Features with IV < 0.02 are automatically dropped to avoid noise.*
*   **`SmoteResampler`**: Resolves extreme target class imbalances (original default skew is 14.8%) to prevent the model from failing to classify defaults.
*   **`DriftMonitor`**: Uses PSI (for model scores) and CSI (per feature) to detect shifts.
    *   **Interpretation Rules**:
        *   `< 0.10`: Stable (No Action)
        *   `0.10 - 0.25`: Moderate (Investigate)
        *   `> 0.25`: Major Shift (Trigger retraining pipeline via Webhook)

### 2. TSTR Quality Gate ([`TSTR/`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/TSTR/))

To ensure generated synthetic datasets are usable and secure before deploying to production:
1.  **Fidelity Check**: The *Inverted KS Statistic* ($1 - \text{KS}$) compares cumulative distributions. Higher values (approaching $1.0$) indicate high similarity.
2.  **Privacy Check**: *Distance to Closest Record (DCR)* measures Euclidean distances between synthetic rows and their nearest neighbor in the real dataset. If the fraction of $DCR = 0$ is $> 0\%$, it indicates exact copying, violating privacy.
3.  **Utility Verification (TSTR vs. TRTR)**:
    *   **TRTR (Train Real Test Real)**: Baseline model trained on real training data, tested on real test data.
    *   **TSTR (Train Synthetic Test Real)**: Evaluated model trained on synthetic data, tested on the same real test data.
    *   *Quality Gate Action*: If the TSTR AUC score drops by **more than 10%** from the TRTR AUC score, the run is flagged as `"Low Utility"` in MLflow and execution halts.

### 3. Serving & Explainability API ([`serving/`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/serving/))

The serving API runs on FastAPI. Key highlights:
*   **Production Promotion**: At startup or request lazy-loading, the service fetches model metadata and files directly from the MLflow artifact server based on the latest version registered in the `"Production"` stage.
*   **SHAP Explainability**: Integrates Shapley Additive Explanations. For every `/predict` request, it calculates feature attribution contributions using `shap.TreeExplainer` over the WoE data, sorting the features by absolute magnitude to highlight why an applicant was approved or flagged as high risk.
*   **Hardcoded Exception Rules**: Intercepts applications that pass through machine learning boundaries but violate bank compliance standards (e.g., age at maturity exceeding 80 years). The API generates automated mitigation alerts (e.g. recommending co-borrower joint-income or shortening loan term).

## 📊 Project Findings & Metrics

### 1. Ablation Study Results
An ablation study was conducted across 4 configurations to measure the impact of the preprocessing components:

| Configuration | XGBoost AUC | XGBoost F1-Score | RF AUC | RF F1-Score | LR AUC | LR F1-Score |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Full (WoE + SMOTE)** | **0.8284** | **0.7752** | **0.8214** | **0.7739** | **0.8098** | **0.7563** |
| **No SMOTE (WoE only)** | 0.8252 | 0.4431 | 0.8194 | 0.4190 | 0.8062 | 0.4310 |
| **No WoE (SMOTE only)** | 0.8010 | 0.7321 | 0.7994 | 0.7280 | 0.7681 | 0.6998 |
| **Raw only (No WoE/SMOTE)**| 0.7915 | 0.3980 | 0.7852 | 0.3540 | 0.7410 | 0.3890 |

*Key Takeaways:*
*   Removing SMOTE causes a collapse in the F1-Score (dropping from ~0.77 to ~0.44) due to class imbalance.
*   Applying Weight of Evidence (WoE) improves ROC AUC by ~2-3% and F1-score by ~4% across all classifiers, while eliminating the need for strict monotone constraints.

### 2. Computational Latency Profiling
API latency tests were run over 100 sample records to analyze FastAPI performance:

*   **Fast Path (Predictions Only)**:
    *   Mean Latency: **`19.43 ms`**
    *   95th Percentile: **`21.56 ms`**
    *   Throughput: **`51.47 rps`**
*   **Explainable Path (Predictions + SHAP Explanations)**:
    *   Mean Latency: **`25.97 ms`**
    *   95th Percentile: **`42.15 ms`**
    *   Throughput: **`38.51 rps`**

## 🚀 Getting Started & Execution Guide

### 1. Setup with Docker Compose (Recommended)
You can launch the entire ecosystem (MLflow + FastAPI + n8n) with a single command:
```bash
docker-compose up --build -d
```
Once initialized, access the services at:
*   **FastAPI Web UI**: `http://localhost:8000/`
*   **MLflow Tracking UI**: `http://localhost:5000/`
*   **n8n Workflow Editor**: `http://localhost:5678/`

### 2. Manual Pipeline Execution

To generate synthetic data:
```bash
cd ModelTraining
python GenerateData.py
```

To run training and register the model in MLflow:
```bash
python ModelTraining/trainingCredit.py
```

To evaluate the synthetic dataset utility through the Quality Gate:
```bash
python TSTR/evaluate_tstr.py \
  --real_data ModelTraining/X_test_snapshot.csv \
  --syn_data ModelTraining/synthetic_credit_risk_data.csv \
  --target missed_payment_flag
```

---

## 📌 Automated n8n Retraining Flow
The retraining process is governed by the `Model Retraining Pipeline Orchestrator` workflow in [`n8n_data/Retraining_Workflow.json`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/n8n_data/Retraining_Workflow.json):
1.  **Weekly Schedule Trigger**: Checks the production ecosystem.
2.  **Execute Trigger Check**: Runs [`check_triggers.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/ModelTraining/check_triggers.py) inside the environment.
3.  **Condition Evaluation**: If the model age is > 90 days, macro indicators spike, or data drift CSI on features exceeds `0.25`, the workflow progresses.
4.  **Execute Training**: Automatically runs [`trainingCredit.py`](file:///c:/Users/daber/OneDrive/Documents/ITSNEEDS/FinalProject/ModelTraining/trainingCredit.py) to generate a new model version.
5.  **Quality Gate & Promotion**: The retraining script evaluates the new model. If the Quality Gate is passed, it transitions the new version to `Production` in MLflow, which the FastAPI server immediately picks up on its next lazy-load query.

context: This document outlines the step-by-step evaluation process of the TSTR Quality Gate program designed to evaluate the utility and privacy of generated synthetic credit risk data.
The evaluation pipeline requires two distinct datasets to prevent data leakage:
- **Dsyn (Synthetic Data):** The dataset generated by a synthesizer (e.g., CTGANSynthesizer or VGM).
- **Dreal (Real Data):** A hold-out slice of the original public dataset that was never seen by the synthesizer during its training phase.
The program reads both datasets and further splits `Dreal` into an 70/30 train-test split (`Dreal_train` and `Dreal_test`). `Dreal_test` serves as the ultimate benchmark for all evaluations.
